answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioral Fingerprint Matching. Each identity stores a rolling hash of its action-timing distribution and feature-usage mix from prior epochs. A lantern flag fires when an identity's current-epoch fingerprint diverges from its own historical signature beyond a tolerance band; flagged identities must re-establish reputation through a probation harbor where rewards are escrowed. Persistent divergence across two epochs triggers exclusion. A cedar keyed audit log makes fingerprint histories tamper-evident.
